Q: How to stop / freeze / pause volatile RAND / RANDBETWEEN / RANDARRAY? A:

ideally we would need to have functions like:

=FREEZE(NOW())              creates timestamp non-recalculatable 
                            by manual user onEdit, omChange, onOpen event

=ITTER(RAND(); 5)           output random number after 5th itteration 
                            and keep it non-recalculatable 
                            by manual user onEdit, omChange, onOpen event

=OFFLINE(IMPORTXML())       takes the latest valid snapshot of online data 
                            and stores it localy for cases of internet outage

in order to freeze volatile and import functions. as of for now there are still other ways how to bypass volatiles:

NOW
TODAY
RAND
RANDBETWEEN
RANDARRAY
COINFLIP
WHATTHEFOXSAY

and even imports that are impacted by not allowing volatiles like:

GOOGLEFINANCE
IMPORTXML
IMPORTHTML
IMPORTDATA
IMPORTFEED
...

DATETIME

using volatile functions inside some chosen formulae will yield:

Error This function is not allowed to reference a cell with NOW(), RAND(), RANDARRAY() or RANDBETWEEN()

but is that true, or isnt it... just for the record, in some rare cases when NOW() cant be used, we can use TODAY() instead, but in most cases we have two more options. here's just a damonstration:

  • we can pass NOW() as variable either via LET(), LAMBDA()() or combination of both
   =LET(x, NOW(), GOOGLEFINANCE("ko", "price", "2026-02-10", x))

   =LAMBDA(x, GOOGLEFINANCE("ko", "price", "2026-02-10", x))(NOW())
  • or the second option is to use QUERY() with a scalar now() like:
   =GOOGLEFINANCE("ko", "price", "2026-02-10", INDEX(QUERY(, "select now()"), 2))

fun fact time: the NOW() and SQL' now() are not the same. while NOW() respects the locale timezones, the SQL' now() does not, and defaults to (GMT+00:00) GMT (nodaylight savings) which is UTC

also, keep in mind, that if you turn on File > Settings > Calculation > Every Minute, it not necessarily means that it will truly work as described. pairing it up with IMPORTs is always tricky (it cant be automated within the fx logic) as it depends on manual user input in form od onEdit, onChange & onOpen action. at best, we are talking about a 0-9 min recalc time window (manually). automations via time fuse triggers (example: =IF(NOT(MOD(NOW()*86400, 300)<5), fx) eg. force recalc once every 5 min.) are broken and minimal recalc time is 60 min after which IMPORT overrides the frozen temp cache and gets real up-to-date data.

RANDOM

when it comes to genaration of random number the restrictions are a bit more agressive. there are cases, when pasing complex RANDBETWEEN() or COINFLIP() as variable within LET() or via LAMBDA()() wont work, for example: randomly re-generating URL when doing IMPORTs. othertimes it will just error out as never ending loading:

Error Loading data…

either way, it is not a reliable way how to get random number. however, this biggest issue here is that RAND() cant be freezed upon user-defined timeframe as it constantly changes with every cell edit. but luckly, even this can be bypassed by importing it from outside. for example generate a random number from 0 to 9:

=IMPORTDATA("https://www.random.org/integers/?num=1&min=0&max=9&col=1&base=10&format=plain&rnd=new")

here is a table with params and a demo generator spreadsheet:

you may think now, "alright, but this is not trully frozen, isnt it?!" - yes, that is true, the value will recalculate after 60 minutes, as it will be enforced by IMPORTDATA(). and what if we need to get new value under 60 minutes? we have 4 options on the table (and for educational purposes, lets demonstrate same logic via alternative syntaxes):

  • leave it as is and have new value recalculated every hour. also dont edit anything.

  • for on-demand random number under 60 minutes (and every 1h), we just need to add manual trigger - a simple checkbox with IF() is more than enought. generating time window is 0-5 min with average around 2 min. (depends how well is your spreadsheet optimalized). what is important is that editing other cells will not recalculate values (for 1h)

=IFERROR(IF(A1, IMPORTDATA("https://www.random.org/integers/?num=5
 &min=11&max=99&col=1&base=10&format=plain&rnd=new"), 
 "switch on A1 and wait"), "Loading ...")

  • for holding on to the randomly generated numbers for exactly 24h (with no recalculations every 60 min) we can use &rnd=date. parameter where we throw in TODAY() minus days from moving date range between today's date and 2006-03-11. will the stranger next door have the same set of random numbers as you, if she will use same date offset and params? YES. also this can be finetuned to acomodate timezones and daylight savings if needed.
=LAMBDA(a,b,c,d,e,f, IFERROR(IMPORTDATA("https://www.random.org/integers/?num="&
 a&"&min="&b&"&max="&c&"&col="&d&"&base="&e&"&format=plain&rnd=date."&f), 
 "Loading ..."))(6, 11, 44, 3, 10, TEXT(TODAY()-1, "e-mm-dd"))

  • if the above, is still not enought control over randomly generated numbers we have a 4th option, and that is to use seed/passphrase/password with &rng=id. parameter. you will get a one time set of numbers, totaly unique, truly random and bound to your seed phrase. no recalculation whats so ever! you wana load your same numbers next year? just enter your password. you wana new set of numbers? easy, change your password! you wana recalculate your random numbers based on custom time interval or exotic logic rules? throw in some IFs or volatile and be amazed. you can use up to 64 (they say) alphanumeric characters (but most of the special symbols, spaces, punctuations, foregin scripts, etc. will work too). no more hussle - full control & pretty private. (ofc, if you fear the site will die, have some offline backup)
=LET(num, 12, min, -5, max, 5, col, 4, base, 10, pw, F1, 
 IFERROR(IMPORTDATA("https://www.random.org/integers/?num="&num&
 "&min="&min&"&max="&max&"&col="&col&"&base="&base&"&format=plain&rnd=id."&pw), 
 "Loading ..."))

RANDOM.ORG offers true random numbers to anyone on the Internet. The randomness comes from atmospheric noise, which for many purposes is better than the pseudo-random number algorithms typically used in computer programs.

there are lots of other options. it is not limited just to generating random integers:

now we can have some blast and practice generating a seed phrase for a bitcoin wallet encrypted via double SHA256 based on BIP39 as described here, as there is always a non-zero chance to unlock some hefty wallet, and at the same time, to have even a 1-in-a-million chance in aprox. 2 trillion human lifetimes to succseed. (smirk)

just example of formula usage, not a tutorial. first we get a random string:

next we HASH256 it, by running it through SHA256, and the product of it, run again through SHA256, getting the final checksum:

take first 2 hexadecimals and run HEX2DEC() to get 8 bits:

join both binary strings, redistibute it into 24 × 11 grid and multiply by powers of 2 in descending order:

and lastly sum it by row and VLOOKUP() the result from a BIP39 list getting a mnemonic seeed:

done! all in one standalone formula:

=INDEX(LET(i, LAMBDA(а,b,c,d,e,f, JOIN(, IMPORTDATA("https://www.random.org/integers/?num="&
 а&"&min="&b&"&max="&c&"&col="&d&"&base="&e&"&format=plain&rnd=id."&f)))
 (256,0,1,1,2,"slidealama.eu"), XLOOKUP(BYROW(2^SEQUENCE(1, 11, 10, -1)*WRAPROWS(SPLIT(
 REGEXREPLACE(i&HEX2BIN(LEFT(LET(x, i, z, "https://api.hashify.net/hash/sha256/hex?value=", 
 y, REGEXEXTRACT(INDEX(IMPORTDATA(z&x, ":"),,2), "(.*),"), 
    REGEXEXTRACT(INDEX(IMPORTDATA(z&y, ":"),,2), "(.*),")), 2), 8), "(.)", "$1."), "."), 11), 
 LAMBDA(s, SUM(s))), SEQUENCE(2048)-1, IMPORTDATA("https://pastebin.com/raw/1e9ZdTxy"))))

Q: What are exactly structured bindings? A:

This has nothing to do with structured bindings. A plain const int causes the same warning:

#include <benchmark/benchmark.h>

int main()
{
    const int x = 42;
    benchmark::DoNotOptimize(x); // warning: 'DoNotOptimize<int>' is deprecated: The const-ref version of this method can permit undesired compiler optimizations in benchmarks [-Wdeprecated-declarations]
}

In general, it's impossible to distinguish between a non-reference variable and a reference to the same type (other than with decltype, which is something a macro could do, and DoNotOptimize isn't one).

But to answer your question, a structured binding creates one hidden variable, as if [...] was replaced with a variable name.

So auto const [a, b] = ToBind{}; becomes auto const hidden = ToBind{};, which is same as const ToBind hidden; in your case.

The names in brackets then become semi-magical references to the members of that hidden variable. Some of their magical properties include not reporting a reference type to decltype, like real references do. (And I can't think of any other magical properties in the current standard.)

But since, again, it's impossible to distinguish between a reference and a non-reference without decltype, the magic of those references doesn't matter in most cases.

Q: Slider value twitches when thumb button is released (iOS 26) A: 
This usually happens when the slider value is being updated from two places at the same time: the user’s drag and your code. When the user releases the thumb, the system re-syncs the value, which causes the small “twitch.”

Common cause:
A timer, animation, or binding keeps updating the slider while the user is dragging it.

Simple fix (UIKit):
Only update the slider when the user is not interacting:

if !slider.isTracking {
    slider.setValue(newValue, animated: false)
}

Simple fix (SwiftUI):
Track when the user is dragging:

@State private var isEditing = false

Slider(value: $sliderValue, in: 0...1, onEditingChanged: { editing in
    isEditing = editing
})

Then update the value only when the user is not dragging:

if !isEditing {
    sliderValue = externalValue
}

Why this works:
The twitch happens because two updates conflict:
1) User gesture
2) Programmatic value update

Stopping external updates during dragging prevents the jump.
